title: CABT: Capacity-Adjusted Benefit-per-Token Prioritization for Throughput-Sensitive Roadmaps
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Existing scoring frameworks (e.g., plain RICE) do not surface the unit economics that matter for inference-first products: per-token cost, latency-sensitive throughput constraints, and reserved GPU capacity implications. Goal: Define a compact, reproducible prioritization rubric that converts feature-level benefits into a normalized per-token benefit and then adjusts by capacity pressure to surface work that delivers the biggest marginal return for constrained serving resources.

CABT overview: Capacity-Adjusted Benefit-per-Token (CABT) is a hybrid scoring method that combines expected customer value, event frequency, and predicted per-request token cost, then penalizes items that increase peak capacity demands (GPU hours) and latency-sensitive tail risks. CABT converts qualitative opportunity descriptions into three normalized inputs: Benefit (B), Token-Weight (T), and Capacity Pressure (C). The final score is: Score = (B / T) * (1 - C_penalty). Higher scores indicate higher priority per unit token consumed. This surfaces features that maximize value while minimizing incremental token spend and capacity churn.

Key definitions: Benefit (B) — numericized expected weekly active user (WAU) or revenue impact translated into a 0-10 scale; Token-Weight (T) — expected median tokens per request * expected weekly volume; Capacity Pressure (C) — a 0-1 factor derived from estimated additional GPU-hours at 95th percentile traffic; C_penalty = min(0.75, alpha * C) where alpha is a tunable sensitivity (default 1.0).

Why CABT: 1) Aligns product trade-offs with Redwood’s core constraints: token cost and dedicated capacity; 2) Enables explicit trade-offs between small high-value features and large token-consuming features; 3) Works well with Dedicated/Private sales where committed capacity drives contractual economics.

Usage guidance: - Translate PM/eng estimates into the three inputs via the CABT intake form (spreadsheet + templates). - Use default alpha=1.0; adjust alpha per cycle if capacity pressure is acute (e.g., before Q4 capacity planning). - Combine CABT with qualitative OKR fit signals: require a binary OKR alignment pass (yes/no) before ranking by CABT. - During cycle planning, produce two ranked lists: CABT-Strict (top by raw CABT score) and CABT-Conservative (apply an extra 15% token tax to any item touching generative scoring paths).

Outputs expected: scoring spreadsheet, worked examples for 10 backlog items, integration doc for roadmap sync, a short training deck for PMs and Solutions Engineering to apply CABT in sales discussions.
